content:
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; increase low-end forecasts, especially for short-term (1-7d) and mid-term (8-15d).
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.00 followed by +0.67), leading to over-forecasting in 10-30d horizon; apply dampening factor of 0.7-0.8 to such peaks.
- Mean reversion is strong in 15-30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; model tends to hold high values; cap forecasts at 1.5x recent 7d average for 15-30d.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.33 or 0.00) followed by a spike, model often fails to adjust; add a 2-3d lag correction to avoid premature recovery.
- For 30d horizon, model frequently overestimates when sentiment is positive in last 3-5 days; apply downward bias of 15-30% if sentiment > 0.67 in last 5 days.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecasts using 3-day moving average for 1-7d horizon.
